artifacts.title: Big Picture: Verifiable Reward RL (RLVR) & GRPO

claims: GRPO eliminates the Value Network critic by normalizing advantages across a sampled group of G candidate rollouts
RLVR replaces learned reward model sycophancy and length-gaming with deterministic programmatic verification
Homogeneous rollout groups naturally emit zero gradient, concentrating compute strictly on the model's active learning boundary
Wen et al. (ICLR 2026) demonstrate that prolonged RLVR training expands reasoning boundaries beyond baseline search compression
Knowledge-to-Verification (K2V) adapts structured checklist verifiers to mitigate reward sparsity in non-coding domains
functions: Algorithmic Comparison Matrix (GRPO vs PPO vs DPO)
The Thinker vs Sampler Debate with Pass@K curves
observable_effects: Switching between Deterministic Sandbox, Subjective RLHF, and Noisy Heuristic verifiers alters the simulated Pass@1 convergence and reward hacking vulnerability
Adjusting group size G from 2 to 32 dynamically updates gradient variance, training stability, and simulated VRAM footprint
Toggling between GRPO and PPO highlights the presence or absence of the separate Value Network and memory overhead

rules: Ground all mathematical equations in peer-reviewed literature (DeepSeekMath, DeepSeek-R1, ICLR 2026)
Explicitly distinguish empirical facts from illustrative browser simulation projections
Highlight failure modes including reward sparsity, verifier bugs, and cold-start exploration failure

objective: Provide an in-depth technical analysis and interactive ablation simulator of Verifiable Reward Reinforcement Learning (RLVR) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), demonstrating why programmatic verifiers and critic-free advantage estimation transformed reasoning models.
audience: AI researchers, machine learning engineers, and system architects
